newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's GTC gets licence to build A-1 motorway.
newsitem.headline: Poland's GTC gets licence to build A-1 motorway.

text.p: Poland's Gdansk Transport Company SA (GTC) received a licence to build the 152-km stretch of the A-1 motorway between the northern cities of Gdansk and Torun, the transport ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
The licence will be handed to GTC on August 25, it said.
The main shareholders of GTC, the sole bidder in the tender, are the Polish construction firm GPRD, cooperative bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA, and U.S.-based Bechtel International Inc.
GPRD's president Zbigniew Wojciechowski earlier said that GPRD and Bechtel Inc, which both have 25-percent stakes in GTC, would be the main firms building the motorway section.
Construction of the Gdansk-Torun motorway, to cost $800 million, will be 85 percent financed by credits, with GTC's own assets contributing 10-15 percent.

Under a government motorway construction programme, firms and consortia are invited by the state Motorway Construction and Exploitation Agency to build sections of a total of 2,500 km of motorways on which they will be allowed to collect tolls.
